limits: COBOL is read as fixed format. Free format files are listed as not parsed.
COPY REPLACING is not applied. A copybook is expanded as written.
A variable call target is resolved only from VALUE clauses and literal MOVEs in the same program.
A called subprogram gets no DDs from its caller's JCL step.
IDCAMS, SORT and other in-stream control cards are not read. Dataset modes on utility steps come from DISP only.
IF/THEN/ELSE and COND= in JCL are not modeled. Step order is file order.
Nested PROC calls and INCLUDE members are not followed. JCL text inside a COBOL literal is noticed, but it makes no edge. A proc or program it names is called unknown, never unreachable.
EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID, START and SEND MAP are not edges.
Only Control-M XML and shell wrappers that name JCL files are read as schedulers.
DCB, LRECL and RECFM are not read, so a record length on a DD is not compared with a copybook.
A contract edge is high when both sides COPY the same layout. A program can COPY a layout and still read the record through a private one, so high means shared layout, not proven equal.
LINK and XCTL are both call edges. XCTL never returns, and control flow is not modeled.

dead_code_reasons.PGMDEAD: no static path from any entry point and no reachable computed call in the tree
dead_code_reasons.cpy:UNUSED: no static path from any entry point and no reachable computed call in the tree

analysis.structure_basis: programs reachable from an entry point (2 of 3)
analysis.articulation_basis: call edges between programs plus data edges from programs to datasets

wave_seed.basis: family of the entry points that use a unit, in a fixed order. Facts only, no risk judgment.

waves.description: Batch jobs that run application programs and write nothing another entry point uses

unassigned.reason: dead code candidate, unreachable. See dead-code.json.

warnings: No last-modified dates exist (the target is not a git repository, or --no-git was used). The dormant bucket was NOT computed. An empty dormant list means not measured.
1 JCL job(s) are in the tree but no scheduler artifact was parsed. The order jobs run in across jobs is unknown. Ask for the scheduler export.
